name: Mystery
description: Whodunit and puzzle stories that challenge viewers to solve the mystery before the reveal
image_style: noir detective style digital art, moody atmospheric lighting, deep shadows, muted color palette with selective color highlights, cinematic mystery composition, detailed environments, intrigue
negative_prompt: bright cheerful colors, cartoon, childish, anime, sunny, low quality, blurry, flat lighting
script_system_prompt: You write scripts for mystery videos that turn viewers into detectives. Every clue you plant matters. You use misdirection skillfully — red herrings that feel fair in hindsight. The viewer should be able to solve it if they pay close attention, but most won't. You always reply with valid JSON only.
script_user_template:
Write a mystery story video script.

Premise: "{topic}"
Number of scenes: {scenes}

Rules:
- HOOK: Scene 1 presents the mystery — something is wrong, someone is missing, a crime has been committed. Make it specific and intriguing.
- Scenes 2-5: Drop clues one per scene. Each clue should point toward the truth BUT also support at least one wrong conclusion. Include one clear red herring.
- Include a "pause and think" moment: "Can you figure it out? The answer is in the next scene."
- The reveal: second-to-last scene reveals the truth. It must feel surprising but fair — every clue supported it.
- The final scene shows the aftermath and adds one last detail that makes the viewer rethink everything.
- Narration is 2-3 sentences per scene (about 15 seconds). Build suspense with pacing.
- speaker: "narrator" for investigation, "character_1"/"character_2" for witness statements or dialogue.
- image_prompt: noir/mystery aesthetic, atmospheric, show clues and suspicious details. No text.
- mood: one of "intriguing", "suspicious", "tense", "revealing", "shocking", "satisfying"

Reply with JSON in exactly this shape:
{
  "title": "mysterious YouTube title under 70 characters",
  "description": "2-3 sentences that hook without spoiling",
  "tags": ["mystery", "detective", "whodunit", "..."],
  "scenes": [
    {"narration": "...", "image_prompt": "...", "speaker": "narrator", "mood": "intriguing"}
  ]
}
